comparison_scale.metric: unweighted sum of log predictive probabilities on the common held-out block
comparison_scale.why_it_matters: Comparing raw decay-weighted likelihood sums would favour the longest half-life purely because its total observation weight is larger. The implemented metric removes that confound by scoring all candidates unweighted on identical ticks.

findings.method: For each candidate half-life H the local deviations u are fitted on all transitions EXCEPT the most recent block, then scored by an UNWEIGHTED predictive log likelihood on that held-out recent block; the candidate weights are a softmax of those scores and the reported prediction is a probability-weighted average of the full-history fits.

no_future_information.note: The scoring block is strictly later in tick order than the fitting block, so each historical forecast is generated before its own target outcome is observed.

same_eligible_ticks.derived_from: tick order only, so identical across all candidate half-lives
same_eligible_ticks.holdout_rule: min(40, max(8, n // 3)) most recent transitions by actual tick

support_and_weights.weight_definition: 2 ** (-(cutoff - 1 - tick) / H); equals 1 at tick cutoff-1

uncertainty.caveat: Regularization reduces effective complexity below the 37 nominal parameters, and nonstationarity plus the Laplace approximation also contribute error. These numbers describe local estimation uncertainty; they do not by themselves prove the remaining gap is variance rather than bias or approximation error.
